reply.summary: Researched ADR-014 (profiles as chains) and wrote docs/designs/014-profiles-as-chains/01-research.md. Verified the shipped chain substrate on main (profile/v1 closed entry set, resolve_chain with MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH=32 and Cycle/ChainTooDeep, per-format version gate, conformance harness round-trip and zero-fixture rules, parse budgets) and mapped the open v2 work against prior art and standards: git rebase, quilt, Nix overlays, systemd drop-ins, Steam Input action set layers, RFC 6902 JSON Patch and RFC 7396/7386 JSON Merge Patch, with security-landscape evidence (billion laughs, CVE-2022-28948, toml-rs recursion advisories, TF2 config-chain hangs and 1 MiB exec-bypass). Key risks flagged: single-document-only cycle/depth guards before cross-file resolution exists, undefined mixed-major chains, delta-list encoding under the table-free grammar, kind/derives contradiction, unstated composite chain budget, and the re-pinned-base drift with no named failure mode. Every claim carries its source URL or repo path inline; three lenses applied (Prior art, Standards, Security landscape).
reply.commitMessage: docs: add research artifact for profiles-as-chains (014)
docs: add design proposal for ADR-014 profiles as chains

findings.location: Chain operations: `fork`, `diff`, `merge` — fork bullet: "empty delta lists for the caller to fill"; contradicts The contract per-link rule "A `patch` has non-empty `derives` and at least one element across `set`/`clear`/`swap`" and invalid fixture `patch-empty-deltas.toml`; also Test strategy #5 "`resolve(fork(a) + diff, manifest)` equals `resolve(b, manifest)`"
findings.problem: fork's output is always a patch with zero delta elements, which the v2 grammar refuses at parse, so the one chain operation ADR-014 Decision Three names never returns a document that parses, re-parses, or loads; the round-trip property test composes that illegal document.
findings.fix: Either state that fork returns a not-yet-loadable shell and pin it (Test #5: fork's output refuses to load until the caller adds a delta; the round-trip property appends `diff` to `a` alone, dropping `fork(a) +`), or give fork the caller's first delta elements so its output is a valid patch.

findings.location: Chain operations: `merge` — "When no such patch exists — one side clears an action the other sets, an order the fixed list order cannot express — `merge` refuses the whole result"; Test strategy #5 "conflicting patches (clear vs set on one action) refuse the whole merge"
findings.problem: Clear-vs-set on one action is expressible as one patch under the design's own determinism rules (fixed order set → clear → swap, last write wins): upper patch clears → emit `clear X`, upper patch sets → emit `set X i`. The stated predicate therefore refuses merges the same paragraph promises are fine ("Compatible overlaps are not conflicts") and contradicts the Options criterion "a conflict is representable iff the composed effect cannot be written as one patch"; Test #5 pins the wrong case.
findings.fix: State the predicate as per-action non-representability under the fixed order and use an example that has no one-patch form — lower patch `clear X`, upper patch `swap X Y` with Y bound: the net "X takes Y's binding, Y unbound" requires a swap before a clear, which the order forbids — and re-word Test #5 to that pair.

findings.location: Chain operations: `diff` bullet "Its output is a v2 patch document (the diff *is* the grammar) that `resolve`s to exactly what it must"; same shape in the `merge` bullet
findings.problem: When the two chains resolve to the same layout (b is a, or a plus a self-cancelling patch) diff emits zero elements, which the `patch-empty-deltas.toml` rule refuses; merge of two mutually inverse swap patches composes to the identity, same illegal shape. Two of the three operations are undefined on legal input.
findings.fix: One clause each reusing the existing refusal: diff refuses when the two resolved layouts are equal, naming both heads; merge refuses an identity composition.

findings.location: Resolution — "Mount at any rung" paragraph: "a consumer takes a prefix, a suffix, or the documents singly. The chain is only meaningful whole, so a suffix without its base is refused by `load_chain` at load"
findings.problem: The sentence grants a suffix and the very next sentence refuses it, so the paragraph both allows and forbids the same read, leaving the ADR Decision Three mount-at-any-rung requirement ambiguous.
findings.fix: Delete "a suffix" (a prefix and single documents are what "take its base and patch independently" needs) and let the refusal sentence stand as the rule.

findings.location: Cross-file loading step 3 — "more than `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` links is `ChainTooDeep` — both written against the constant"; Goals "the same guard rules the shipped single-document guard states"; Test strategy #3 "a chain of exactly `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` links resolves and one link more refuses"
findings.problem: The shipped predicate is `derives.len() > MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` (chain.rs:27), so today a head with 32 ancestors (33 resolved links) passes, while the new cross-file boundary test refuses 33. The two layers disagree at exactly one link, so the re-issued `chain-past-max-depth.toml` and the `chain_ops` boundary test can pin different documents.
findings.fix: Name the counted unit once: either "more than `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` ancestor links (the shipped `derives.len() > MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` predicate)", or keep the resolved-links unit and state that the cross-file guard refuses one link earlier than the single-document guard, then write the fixture and the boundary test to that unit.

findings.location: Chain operations signatures — "pub fn merge(p1: &Profile, p2: &Profile) -> Result<Profile, CoreError>" and the diff bullet
findings.problem: The documents diff and merge emit have unspecified `id`, `derives`, and `for`, although those entries are the chain lookup key and file name and must be slug-grammar and collision-free; only fork states the collision rule, so merge/diff output may be unloadable by construction.
findings.fix: One clause each: diff emits `derives = [<a's head id>]` and the joined manifest's pin; merge inherits `id`, `derives`, `for` from p1 and takes a fresh caller-supplied id with fork's collision rule (or refuses when p1 and p2 name the same id).

findings.location: The contract: `schemas/profile/v2/` invalid fixture list — "chain-past-max-depth.toml  self-deriving-chain.toml  table-header.toml  dotted-key.toml …" (no `forged-log-line.toml`); Test strategy #7 "every invalid fixture is refused with a single-line, control-free, truncating message"
findings.problem: The v2 corpus re-issues every v1 grammar fixture except the log-injection one, while v2 refusals echo far more untrusted strings than v1's did (id, derives elements, both pin halves, delta elements, seeded-from, generated-by, ChainLinkMissing's id); `generated-by-control-char.toml` pins the entry's own grammar, not the escape-and-truncate path #7 asserts, so no v2 fixture exercises it.
findings.fix: Re-issue `forged-log-line.toml` at v2 with a `\n`-escaped `generated-by` (or `id`) — the existing fixture mechanism, no new rule.

findings.location: Resolution — "pub struct Chain { pub links: Vec<Profile> }   // deepest base first … head last" and `pub fn resolve(chain: &Chain, manifest: &Manifest)`
findings.problem: A public field makes Chain consumer-buildable: an empty chain (no rule defines its output), a suffix, and a chain whose `kind` positions were never checked all reach resolve/fork/diff, since the completeness and position rules live only inside load_chain.
findings.fix: State that Chain is only ever produced by load_chain (keep `links` private or give a non-public constructor), and state that resolve refuses an empty chain.

findings.location: The model: `document.rs` — "`serialize` writes the ten entries in the fixed order"; Test strategy #6 "a hand-built document carrying all ten entries"
findings.problem: The entry table and the Goals define eleven entries (v1's four plus for, kind, set, clear, swap, seeded-from, generated-by), and the order the sentence itself enumerates names eleven; a wrong count in the section that fixes the closed set propagates to PROFILE_V2_ENTRIES and the grammar_closure.rs expectations.
findings.fix: Change both occurrences to "eleven entries".

findings.location: Cross-file loading / Resolution — "pub fn resolve(chain: &Chain, manifest: &Manifest) -> Result<Vec<ResolvedBinding>, CoreError>" alongside the untouched public `resolve_chain`
findings.problem: The crate will export `resolve_chain` (id-level validation) and `resolve` (delta application), two public names one token apart doing different jobs, and no sentence maps ADR-014 Decision Two's "Resolve the chain with `resolve_chain`" onto the split a reader will notice.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: resolve_chain keeps the id-level validation the ADR names, load_chain walks the files, resolve applies the deltas; consider naming the new one `resolve_layout`.

findings.location: Chosen design → Delta inventory (Edited) — "`PROFILE_ENTRIES` renamed `PROFILE_V1_ENTRIES`, new `PROFILE_V2_ENTRIES`"
findings.problem: The rename is presented as an ordinary edit, but the proposal never states whether PROFILE_ENTRIES is private or part of core's public surface; the zz_api_probe.rs edit is listed for 'the new public names' only, so nothing says whether existing downstream users of the old name break, and the Compatibility matrix has no core-API row.
findings.fix: State in the Edited list (or a matrix row) that the rename is internal because PROFILE_ENTRIES is private — as the assumption register already does for placement::is_slug_name (pub(crate)) — or, if it is public, record the rename as a public-surface break in the matrix; do not add a compat alias.

findings.location: The contract: schemas/profile/v2/ — "The `spec.md` also states the load-level rules below (the directory rule, pin equality, the joins)"
findings.problem: The keyboard-reality check is only half covered: non-ASCII binding names are refused (slug grammar, uppercase fixtures) and named keys are Deferred consistently with the ADR, but chain documents bake input ids like `keyboard:d` into artifacts shared across players (the example carries `set = ["move.steer-left keyboard:d"]`), and nowhere — contract, matrix, or Deferred — is it stated that the physical-key semantics of the closed `keyboard:` vocabulary (character vs position on non-QWERTY layouts) are inherited unchanged from the shipped input/reach-classes contract and are not this design's to define.
findings.fix: One sentence appended to the spec.md load-rule list pinned in Rollout 1: input-id semantics are inherited unchanged from the shipped contract and a chain is layout-neutral data. It adds no mechanism; it clarifies the boundary the determinism rules already assume.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "macOS contributor | no (v1)"
findings.problem: The status cell "no (v1)" is cryptic: a first-time reader cannot tell which posture '(v1)' names or whether a 014-era contribution on macOS is in or out.
findings.fix: Spell the cell out, e.g. "no — outside design 008's supported matrix", and drop the bare "(v1)" marker.

findings.location: Chosen design → Cross-file loading: `load_chain` in `chain_ops.rs` — "Walk `derives` nearest-first: the ancestor `<id>.toml` is looked up *directly in that same directory*" (with "Resolution: deterministic" — "a resolution reads at most `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` (32 MiB) across at most 32 documents")
findings.problem: The walk text is singular but the entry table keeps v1's plural `derives` array ("ancestor chain, nearest first") and `merge` refers to `derives[0]`, so multi-element lists are expected to be legal; nothing states what `derives[1..]` means at v2. Under an untrusted-input format this collapses the design's own mitigation: if the walk follows every element the chain is a tree, `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` no longer bounds documents opened (the ≤32 × 1 MiB figure the Risks row "Cross-file machinery is new attack surface" leans on is false) and "more than `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` links" is left to the implementer, so two implementers disagree about how much hostile input they read. If only `derives[0]` is followed, every later element is an ancestor claim never resolved, so `ChainLinkMissing`'s completeness posture stops covering part of the document.
findings.fix: State one rule at v2: a `patch` has exactly one `derives` element, a `base` none (v1's array untouched per A15/A1; the ADR's "nearest ancestor first" reading survives), pin it with a new `fixtures/invalid/derives-two-elements.toml`, and rewrite the composite-cost sentence to count documents opened per resolution under that rule. Alternative if the array stays: say all elements are followed, give the walk a visited-set plus a documents-opened counter, and replace the ≤32 × 1 MiB sentence with the resulting bound — do not leave both readings available.

findings.location: Chosen design → Cross-file loading: `load_chain` — "the ancestor `<id>.toml` is looked up *directly in that same directory*"
findings.problem: This is the only point where untrusted document content becomes a filesystem path, and the security property is never stated. It holds only incidentally because `derives` elements are slug-grammar-checked at parse (excluding `/`, `.`, `..`); the design never pins the constructed path's parent to the head's directory, never says no other entry may name a location, and Test strategy #3 has no traversal-shaped case — `derives-element-uppercase.toml` tests case, not path.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the load rule: the filesystem path is `<major dir>/<parse-validated slug>.toml`, no other entry names a location, and the constructed path must be a direct child of the head's directory; add the parse case that a `derives` element of `..` or `a/b` refuses as `InvalidValue` (the slug refusal already yields it — name it so a non-Rust implementer conforms).

findings.location: Chosen design → Cross-file loading / Deferred — "A hub upload bundle is exactly such a directory (ADR-018 ships the transport; this is the shape it transports"
findings.problem: The only source classified as untrusted is `data/profiles/` (A12; Risks says "`data/profiles/` posture unchanged"). This design defines a second, network-sourced input — a directory of chain documents arriving from a hub — and writes `load_chain(head: &Path)` for a third, a player's personal chain directory; neither is classified. (Deferring trust-over-a-channel to ADR-018 is consistent with the ADR's Decision Four and Consequences, so this is not re-opening a deferral — it is the missing classification of sources whose guards are decided here.)
findings.fix: One sentence where the bundle shape is recorded (or in A12's row): every document `load_chain` opens — fixtures, `data/profiles/`, a hub bundle directory, a personal chain directory — is parsed under the same version gate, byte budget and chain guards, source-independent; trust stays with validation and explicit adoption.

findings.location: Chosen design → Chain operations — "`diff` requires the two chains to share their deepest link id — the same base"
findings.problem: Base identity is the id string, not the document. Chains loaded from different directories can name the same base id with different bytes (the id↔filename rule is unique only within one directory), so `diff` asserts a property — "the chain `a` extended by the diff resolves to `b`'s resolved layout" — that is false for a consumer applying the emitted patch over its own base, and pin equality at load will not catch it because the ids match. `diff`'s output is precisely the artifact that gets shared.
findings.fix: Make the shared-base test content-bearing: require the deepest link's parsed `Profile` (or its `serialize` bytes) to be equal for both chains, refusing with a named error when the ids match and the documents differ, and state that in the `diff` bullet instead of "share their deepest link id".

findings.location: Entry table / Provenance labels — "`generated-by` | string | no | 1–128 octets, no ASCII control characters: a label naming what produced the document"
findings.problem: This is the format's only free-text field and the checklist's "what may be logged, what leaves the machine when bindings are shared" is unanswered for it. It is exported with the document in the bundle shape defined here, echoed into logs via the `one_line` path on every refusal (A13), and its grammar allows arbitrary non-ASCII, so it can carry a personal name or email or a bidi-override/homoglyph string that renders as an authority name in a UI. Decision Four bounds the damage but does not make the label non-public or non-spoofable.
findings.fix: Add one sentence in Provenance labels: the label is a public, shared artifact, must not be treated as secret or displayed as authority, and reaches logs only through `one_line`; tighten the grammar to exclude default-ignorable and bidi control characters, reusing the existing `generated-by-control-char.toml` fixture shape.

findings.location: Chosen design → Cross-file loading: `load_chain` in `chain_ops.rs`, step 2, with the Resolution paragraph — "Walk `derives` nearest-first: the ancestor `<id>.toml` is looked up *directly in that same directory*" / "a resolution reads at most `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH × MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` (32 MiB) across at most 32 documents"
findings.problem: The composite load bound counts documents, but the document never states that the walk is a single path. `derives` is inherited from v1 as an array of ancestors, nearest first (A1, A15), the model keeps `derives: Vec<String>`, and A6 records that nothing bounds array sizes — so one 1 MiB document can carry tens of thousands of ancestor ids. Whether `load_chain` follows `derives[0]` only, follows every element, or refuses extras is unstated, and the design requires `spec.md` to carry the load-level rules so a non-Rust implementer can conform; such an implementer reading "an array of ancestors, nearest first" will traverse all of them, evading the "at most 32 documents" bound through file references — the exact mechanism the design's own prior-art finding names ("TF2 shows per-file caps evaded once files reference files", A20).
findings.fix: In `load_chain` step 2 add one clause fixing the walk's shape: the walk follows `derives[0]` only; any further element is carried as data and never traversed (state refusal instead if that is the intent). Restate the composite as "`≤ MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` documents opened per resolution, regardless of `derives` array length". This replaces the implicit reading; it adds no mechanism and no new cap.

findings.location: Options → "Composite chain budget", Chosen design → The contract → Delta elements ("the cap the manifest row cap already prices"), Resolution composite paragraph, and Chain operations → `diff`/`merge`
findings.problem: The claim that cost "is bounded and now stated" stops at bytes, link count and per-list count. It omits the derived totals that drive `resolve`'s work (≤ 32 links × 3 lists × 256 = 24,576 delta elements per chain; resolved bindings ≤ the joined manifest's action-row count) and never quantifies the "manifest row cap" it justifies the 256 cap by mirroring. That number is load-bearing for the chain operations: `diff` emits one element per differing/unbound action and `merge` composes "over every action either touches", so their outputs are capped only while the manifest row cap ≤ `MAX_PATCH_DELTA_ELEMENTS`. The Risks table prices raising the delta cap but not the opposite direction, which would let `diff`/`merge` emit documents that fail the design's own per-list parse rule — a case with no stated refusal and no case in Test strategy #5.
findings.fix: Name the manifest row-cap constant with its value at first use, add the derived element total to the composite sentence, and add one clause to the `diff`/`merge` bullets that their output obeys `MAX_PATCH_DELTA_ELEMENTS` because the joined action table is capped, with a refusal if that ever stops holding.

findings.location: Chosen design → Resolution → Load-time joins ("every action id in any `set`/`clear`/`swap` must be a row of that manifest's `actions` table") and determinism rule 3 ("`set` replaces any binding for that action (last writer wins)")
findings.problem: The load-path cost depends on representation, and the document fixes only ordering, which pushes toward arrays: the action table's "row order is data" (rule 5), deltas apply sequentially in array order, and `fork` is "refused if it collides with any link id in the chain". Array membership for the action join, for "any binding for that action", and for `swap`'s two lookups is O(deltas × rows) — bounded but quadratic in the caps (worst case ~6M comparisons per resolution).
findings.fix: One sentence in `resolve`'s contract: action-row membership and the action→binding layout are held in a lookup built once per `load_chain`/`resolve` call, and the manifest's `actions` array order is used only to order output, never for membership. No new mechanism; determinism rule 5 is untouched.

findings.location: Chosen design → Cross-file loading: `load_chain` ("a file whose `id` entry disagrees with its name is `InvalidValue` — the location rule, one rule") and Resolution → Load-time joins ("Manifest identity")
findings.problem: The design states an invalidation rule for only one side of the resolution input: pin equality catches a bumped manifest revision. Nothing covers the other side. Because id↔filename equality is a contract rule and links are looked up by id in one directory, a consumer (ADR-017 storage, ADR-018 hub) that identifies a chain by its head id and caches the resolved layout goes stale silently on an in-place link edit under an unchanged pin and unchanged ids. Deferring caching to 017/018 is consistent with the ADR; leaving chain identity undefined is what turns a fast consumer cache into a wrong one.
findings.fix: One line in the `load_chain` section, mirrored in `spec.md` since the spec carries the load rules: a chain's identity is the contents of its link documents — id equality pins the lookup, not the value — and pin equality invalidates only against manifest changes.

findings.location: The contract: `schemas/profile/v2/` — the `id` entry row: "the profile's identifier: slug grammar (A14), ≤ 63 octets"
findings.problem: The 63-octet cap has no stated provenance: it is absent from Options considered, from the assumption register (A14 cites the shared slug grammar with no length cap), and from Rollout 2's named budget constants (`MAX_PATCH_DELTA_ELEMENTS`, `MAX_GENERATED_BY_OCTETS`) — yet it is enforced via the entry table, the Id grammars rule, `id-past-cap.toml`, and Test strategy #1. The cap itself traces to the profile-id↔file-name directory rule, so this is a traceability gap, not YAGNI: the number is unowned and unjustified in the text.
findings.fix: One line: if the cap mirrors a cap already shipped for manifest/preset ids, add that citation to A14's basis; if it is new, name it beside the two rollout constants or state the in-text reason (the directory rule wants a bounded path segment).

reply.summary: All four majors are consumed by changing the design, not appending to it: security/performance majors (derives-array ambiguity) are resolved by one new rule — a v2 `patch` carries exactly one `derives` element and a `base` none, pinned by `derives-two-elements.toml`, making the walk a single path and the ≤`MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH`-documents bound true — while the re-issued `chain-past-max-depth.toml` fixture and the Goals claim about it are deleted (depth now pinned only by `chain_ops` tests, unit named once); correctness major 1 is fixed by stating `fork`'s empty-delta shell is unloadable until filled and recomposing the round-trip over `a + diff` (diff's output now pins `id`/`derives`/`for`); correctness major 2 is fixed by restating `merge`'s conflict as per-action non-representability under the fixed list order with the `clear X`-under-`swap X Y` example, and Test #5 re-worded to match. The minors landing on the same passages were folded in (one-path walk names the slug-built path and `..`/`a/b` refusals; chain identity is document contents; shared base means the same deepest document; sources share one gate; `generated-by` tightened and pinned as a public label; `Chain` only built by `load_chain`; suffix withdrawn from 'mount at any rung'; 'ten' corrected to eleven; `MAX_MANIFEST_ROWS = 256` named with the derived totals). The diff is net positive (~+40 lines) because the placeholder Revision log grew to its mandated index entries and the three majors each forced a new rule sentence; body additions were offset by deletions (withdrawn fixture and Goals claim, withdrawn suffix clause, merged provenance sentence, compressed load/merge/budget prose).
reply.commitMessage: docs: revise profile-chains proposal for r1 review findings

findings.location: Chain operations — merge bullet: "When some action's composed effect has no one-patch form under the fixed list order — lower `clear X`, upper `swap X Y` with `Y` bound: the net needs the `swap` before the `clear`"; Test strategy #5 "a non-representable pair (a `clear X` under a `swap X Y`) refuses the whole merge"
findings.problem: The pinned example is a representable pair under the design's own rules. The fixed list order is set → clear → swap, so the clear precedes the swap — exactly the composition order of lower-then-upper. If swap exchanges bindings (entry-table reading), the single patch clear=["X"] + swap=["X Y"] reproduces the composed effect on every base layout; if instead "an unbound side stays unbound" makes a half-bound swap a no-op, the composition collapses to clearing X, whose one-patch form is clear=["X"]. Under either reading merge must emit a patch, so the text and Test #5 refuse something the stated criterion (Options: "a conflict is representable iff the composed effect cannot be written as one patch") composes. The predicate and the set-under-clear clause are now correct; only the exemplar (which my own r1 fix supplied, backwards) and the test case remain wrong.
findings.fix: Swap the pair: lower `swap X Y`, upper `clear X` (both actions bound in the base) — the net is X unbound and Y bound to X's former, base-dependent input, which needs the clear after the swap (forbidden by the fixed order) and cannot be named by `set`; mirror the same flipped pair in Test #5.

findings.location: Chain operations — merge bullet: "emits one patch producing that composition on the base" (no identity case)
findings.problem: The identity half of the r1 empty-output edge is still open: two identical swap patches (`swap X Y` under `swap X Y`) compose to the identity, whose only one-patch form is the empty patch that `patch-empty-deltas` refuses. diff gained "chains resolving to equal layouts refuse too" but merge states no refusal and Test #5 has no case, so merge can return a document the grammar will not accept.
findings.fix: One clause: a composition that cancels to the identity refuses as the empty-patch case; add the matching clause to Test #5.

findings.location: Cross-file loading — "pub struct Chain { links: Vec<Profile> }  // only load_chain builds one" vs Resolution "a consumer takes a prefix or the documents singly" and Test strategy #5 "appending its output to `a` resolves to `resolve(b, manifest)`"
findings.problem: The revised private `links` with no public constructor closes the buildability hole but strands the promised consumer access: with no accessor named anywhere, neither a consumer taking a prefix/singles from a returned Chain nor the integration test building the chain `a + diff` is expressible through the public surface.
findings.fix: Either add a read-only accessor (`pub fn links(&self) -> &[Profile]`, construction still only via `load_chain`, and name it in the `zz_api_probe` list), or restate the mount route and Test #5 as file-level moves (prefix = `load_chain` of the lower link as head, singly = `parse_file`, round-trip = write diff's output into the directory and `load_chain` it as the new head).

findings.location: The contract — `generated-by` row: "no ASCII control, default-ignorable, or bidi-control characters"
findings.problem: The rule widened to two new refused classes while the per-link promise "each with a named fixture above" is backed only by `generated-by-control-char.toml` for the ASCII-control branch.
findings.fix: Extend that fixture or name one more (e.g. a bidi-bearing label) so each refused class has a fixture.

findings.location: Chain operations — diff and merge bullets: "(`fork`'s collision rule)"
findings.problem: fork's collision rule is "refused if it collides with any link id in the chain", but merge takes no chain and diff takes two; the set of ids the caller's `id` must not hit is unspecified.
findings.fix: One parenthetical each naming the set: merge — `p1` and `p2` ids; diff — every link id of `a` (and optionally of `b`).

findings.location: Provenance labels / The contract entry table — "`generated-by` | string | no | 1–128 octets, no ASCII control, default-ignorable, or bidi-control characters"
findings.problem: The r1 closure adds two new character classes to the label grammar but neither is defined nor pinned: the invalid-fixture list still names only `generated-by-past-cap.toml` and `generated-by-control-char.toml`, and Test strategy #1 still tests only "`generated-by` past 128 octets or control-character-bearing". The compatibility matrix makes `profile/v2/spec.md` + fixtures the whole contract for a "Third-party reader, non-Rust", so an undefined Unicode class with no fixture leaves two implementers free to disagree about whether a bidi override or a default-ignorable codepoint in a label is refused — the renders-as-authority case the ban was added to close (checklist: what may be logged / what leaves the machine when bindings are shared).
findings.fix: Extend the existing pair with one fixture carrying a bidi formatting character (or add `generated-by-bidi-control.toml`) and name it in Test #1's `generated-by` clause, and state the classes in the entry row implementably without a Unicode table: `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point` plus the explicit ranges U+202A–U+202E and U+2066–U+2069. No mechanism changes; this pins the rule the revision added.

findings.location: Cross-file loading: `load_chain` in `chain_ops.rs`, step 2 — "the constructed path is always a direct child of the head, `<major dir>/<parse-validated slug>.toml`" and "mirroring `load_manifest`'s id↔directory equality, which pins the lookup but not the value"
findings.problem: Two wording slips in the sentence that now carries the path-containment property: "a direct child of the head" names a document where a directory is meant, and "but not the value" follows immediately after a rule whose subject is the `id` value, so it can be read as waiving the id↔filename check that stops one file answering for another link's id.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "a direct child of the head's directory", and replace "which pins the lookup but not the value" with "which pins the lookup, not the document: equal ids in different directories are not the same link" — the sentence's own closing clause ("a chain's identity is its documents' contents") already states that.

findings.location: Chain operations → `diff`/`merge` — "`diff` … a `set` per differing action, a `clear` per action `b` unbinds" and "`merge` … composes the two delta lists in chain order … over every action either touches"

findings.location: crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:763 (emit_composition, 746-789)
findings.problem: The `exchanged` partner guard tests the wrong key (`exchanged.contains(other)` while the code inserts `action`), so the second half of any reciprocal base-binding pair always hits `composition_fault`. `emitted.swap` can therefore never be non-empty: every `merge` whose composed result keeps a net exchange refuses as a conflict, including plainly compatible ones where the two patches touch disjoint actions (`p1 = swap a b`, `p2 = set c k` must merge into one patch with `set [c k]` + `swap [a b]`). That contradicts the proposal's merge contract ("Compatible overlaps are not conflicts", deterministic element order including swap elements) and breaks ADR-014 Decision Three's `merge` for a whole input class. No test sees it: no merge test asserts a non-empty `swaps_of(&merged)` (chain_ops.rs:1984 asserts it empty), and the two swap-carrying merge tests (:2017, :2046) expect a refusal either way.
findings.fix: Refuse only on a non-reciprocal composition and skip the partner of an already-emitted pair: `if !reciprocal { return Err(composition_fault(action, other)); } if exchanged.contains(other) { continue; } exchanged.insert(action.clone()); emitted.swap.push((action.clone(), other.clone()));`. Add the missing pin: `p1 = swap a b` with `p2 = set c k` (or `clear d`) merges to one patch carrying the swap plus the second patch's element, and resolves over the base to the same layout as the two-patch chain; keep the `swap X Y` under `clear X` case refusing via the `!reciprocal` branch.

findings.location: crates/core/src/error.rs:141
findings.problem: A shipped refusal string was edited to satisfy a new test: `CoreError::Cycle`'s Display text gained "(`Cycle`)". The proposal states "No `CoreError` variant is removed or changed; one is added", the compatibility matrix pins existing `resolve_chain` refusals as untouched, and A15 pins the shipped guard as delivered. The only driver is the needle list in the new assertion at crates/core/tests/chain_ops.rs:1281 (`["Cycle", "link-a", "link-b"]`), which the original message cannot satisfy — and which no message can satisfy for the two link ids since `Cycle` carries no payload, so the test passes on the `"Cycle"` needle alone via `assert_refusal_names`' `any()`. A frozen contract string should not move to make a test green.
findings.fix: Revert the arm to `write!(f, "chain derives from itself")` and drop `"Cycle"` from that needle list; the variant is already asserted at chain_ops.rs:1277-1280, which is what Test strategy #3 pins.

findings.location: crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:394-408 (check_link_version); test comment at crates/core/tests/chain_ops.rs:1404-1427
findings.problem: The proposal's Options says the one-directory rule "reuses `check_dir_version` (A5)". The code re-implements it and answers `UnsupportedVersion` naming profile's majors, while every shipped loader applying this same rule answers `InvalidValue` (document.rs:1337-1352 via reach.rs:160, placement.rs:160, action.rs:235-241) — the rule the codebase keeps as one definition precisely so loaders "cannot drift into two spellings of it" (document.rs:1354-1358). The new test's doc comment claims the chain refuses "exactly as the shipped loaders already refuse it (`reach_v2.rs`)", which is false: reach_v2.rs:626-657 pins `InvalidValue` for the identical fault. It fails closed either way, so this is contract consistency plus a wrong comment.

findings.location: crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:334-335 with inherit_provenance at :650-656
findings.problem: `merge` copies `seeded-from`/`generated-by` from the operands onto the merged document — behavior the proposal's merge contract never asks for (it pins only id, inherited derives/for, and the composed delta lists). `generated-by` means "a label naming what produced the document", so carrying p1's label asserts that whatever produced p1 produced the merge result: a false fact in a label the design insists is never displayed as authority (ADR-014 Decision Four).
findings.fix: Leave both provenance labels absent on merge output, or add the inheritance rule to the proposal with a test stating which operand is inherited and why.

findings.location: crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:118-119 with open_link at :347-352
findings.problem: `load_chain` applies the missing-link rule to the head as well, so a missing head answers `ChainLinkMissing { id: <file stem> }`. The proposal's step 1 is `parse_file(head)` and A13 assigns read failures to `Io`, whose variant carries the path for `source_path`; `ChainLinkMissing` deliberately omits the path, so a consumer cannot log which head was missing, and the echoed value is a raw, grammar-unvalidated file stem rather than a profile id. The ancestor rule A18 is about is correct and pinned (:348-351, tests/chain_ops.rs:1322-1346).
findings.fix: Resolve the head through `parse_file` (its `Io` already carries the path) and apply `ChainLinkMissing` only to links the walk constructed from a `derives` element.

findings.location: crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:714-738 (apply_lists)
findings.problem: `Binding::Base` is never unbound, so the symbol model always moves a `swap` while `resolve`'s rule 3 makes it a no-op when a side is unbound. The effect is over-refusal only (`p1 = set X a`, `p2 = swap X Y` refuses, although over a base leaving Y unbound the composition is just `set X a`), and the comment says the assumption is deliberate — but the proposal says merge composes "exactly, not heuristically" and never states the assumption.
findings.fix: State it in one sentence of the merge section ("the base is assumed to bind both sides of an exchange; a merge that would need otherwise refuses") so the refusal is predictable to a third-party implementer.

findings.location: crates/core/src/document.rs:639
findings.problem: The proposal says the v2 writer "branches on `version` alone", but `serialize_profile_link` skips `kind` and `for` when `kind` is `None`. Unreachable from a parse, but `Profile`'s fields are public, so a consumer can build a v2 model with `kind: None` and get text that will not re-parse — the one case the function's own doc comment promises not to produce.
findings.fix: Write `kind`/`for` unconditionally on the v2 branch and document that a v2 model must carry a kind, or state the precondition in the doc comment.

findings.location: crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:347-375 (open_link: try_exists at :348, id check at :363-373; lookup built at :131, stem at :379)
findings.problem: The id↔file-name equality rule compares the document's declared `id` with the stem of the path `load_chain` itself constructed, never with the name the filesystem matched. On a case-insensitive filesystem (the matrix's Windows row, 'Supported? yes'), a directory holding `Game-Base.toml` with `id = "game-base"` satisfies a `derives = ["game-base"]` lookup and loads, while the same chain refuses `ChainLinkMissing` on the Linux CI runner. The Windows matrix row rests on 'profile-id ↔ file-name equality is case-unique', which the loader does not enforce in that direction; no test pins a case-only mismatch (tests/chain_ops.rs:1354 differs by more than case), and the Windows leg of Test strategy #9 is the one leg that would miss it.
findings.fix: Pin the byte-exact on-disk name before opening the link: in `open_link`, require `fs::read_dir(directory)` to contain an entry whose `file_name()` equals `{expected}.toml` byte-for-byte (one scan per link, inside the existing MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH budget), and add the case-only mismatch to the load_chain guard cases (Test strategy #3). Alternatively state the caveat contract-side — one sentence in schemas/profile/v2/spec.md §'Loading a chain' rule 3 plus the matrix's Windows row — but the platform divergence must be refused or written down, not left implicit.

findings.location: schemas/profile/v2/spec.md:46 and §Per-link rules; enforcing code crates/core/src/document.rs:1074 (check_generated_by) with is_label_char at :1101
findings.problem: spec.md states the `generated-by` character rule as 'no ASCII control or bidi-control characters', but the reference reader also refuses the default-ignorable/joiner set the proposal names (soft hyphen, U+034F, U+061C, U+180E-180F, U+200B-200F, U+202A-202E, U+2060-206F, U+FEFF, U+FFF9-FFFB). Only the two halves the spec states are corpus-pinned (generated-by-control-char.toml, generated-by-bidi-char.toml — the latter's comment asserts the default-ignorable rule, which is not contract text), and no fixture or test carries a non-ASCII label at all, so the accept side of the boundary is unpinned too. Under the matrix's 'third-party reader, non-Rust — spec.md + fixtures are the contract' row, a conforming reader accepts documents bindforge-core refuses.

Keep the design's fixture list as written; if the panel prefers corpus pins (generated-by-soft-hyphen.toml, a valid unicode-label fixture), edit the design's fixture list in the same PR.

findings.location: crates/core/src/document.rs:1051 (check_profile_slug), used as a file name at crates/core/src/chain_ops.rs:131 and :348; fresh ids via chain_ops.rs:581
findings.problem: The slug grammar admits Windows reserved device basenames (`con`, `aux`, `prn`, `nul`, `com1`-`com9`, `lpt1`-`lpt9`), which on Windows are not file names: they cannot be created, git refuses to check them out, and Path::try_exists answers through the device. A chain with `id = "con"` loads on Linux and is unbuildable/unfetchable for the Windows contributor the matrix marks supported, and a hub bundle could carry one. Nothing in the diff addresses it. Precedent note: placement::is_slug_name already turns manifest and geometry ids into path components with the same grammar and no guard, so this is a widening of existing exposure, not new.
findings.fix: Decide it once where the grammar lives: either reject a reserved Windows basename inside check_profile_slug (naming the rule, with a grammar/chain_ops case pinning it) and open the same question for placement::is_slug_name as a follow-up, or record it under Deferred/out of scope with an owner and add one sentence to spec.md §'Id grammars' plus the matrix's Windows row that the id grammar does not exclude platform-reserved names.

findings.location: crates/core/src/document.rs:1101-1116 (is_label_char); escape side at crates/core/src/error.rs:173
